recentItems.title: Bail application of Lucas Legabe
recentItems.description:
The bail application of a businessman accused in the theft of a multimillion-rand cocaine consignment from a Hawks facility in KZN continues today in the Port Shepstone Magistrates' Court.

Lucas Legabe faces charges of housebreaking with intent to steal and dealing in drugs. 

The state says it intends to strongly oppose bail. Credit: Taliesha Naidoo

recentItems.title: Massive disruption hits UK airports after air traffic control technical fault
recentItems.description:
Flights at major British airports were disrupted by a technical fault at air traffic control provider NATS, the latest in a series of failures that has renewed questions about the resilience of Britain's aviation infrastructure.

The hours-long shutdown resulted in the cancellation of more than 1 000 flights and and left hundreds of passengers stranded. 

The shutdown comes three years after the last system meltdown in August 2023.

For more, we cross to SABC News Correspondent John Bevir in Bristol in the United Kingdom. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa on the campaign trail in Ekurhuleni
recentItems.description:
ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa is on the campaign trail in Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg as we edge closer to the polls.

The party is also preparing for an electoral court bid over its candidates that could not be captured on the IEC's Online Candidate Nomination System.

The ANC's case will be heard on September 15.

For more on this we cross live to our reporter Samkele Maseko

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Police and Education MEC lead schools raid
recentItems.description:
Twenty-three schools in Gauteng have been targeted so far in the ongoing unannounced search-and-seizure school safety operation.

Led by the South African Police Service - alongside Gauteng Education MEC Lebogang Maile - these raids are being conducted to strengthen school safety, curb criminality, and combat gangsterism, substance abuse, and the possession of dangerous weapons. SABC News Reporter, Nomvuyo Ntanjana is there live.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Anele Tembe murder case postponed to the 19th of October
recentItems.description:
The inquest into the death of 22-year-old Anele Tembe has been postponed to the 19th of October at the Cape Town Magistrates Court. Tembe, who was engaged to late rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes’ fell from the 10th floor of a hotel. 

The court heard testimony today about events surrounding Tembe’s alleged fall. Three witnesses testified to the court, speaking of what was heard and observed in the moments before and after the fall, including reports of a distressed woman’s voice, followed by a loud bang and a man repeatedly shouting “oh my god” in shock. 

The court also heard that alcohol was still being ordered from the hotel room after moments after Tembe’s fatal fall.  Credit: Mlamli Maneli

recentItems.title: 2026 Municipal Polls | IEC introduces new Disinformation Code
recentItems.description:
The Electoral Commission has introduced its new Disinformation Code ahead of the 2026 Local Government Elections.

The Code sets out the rules ahead of the November 4th polls, and forms part of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

Today, we get to unpack this code further with Elections Analyst, Paul Berkowitz on our video link.

recentItems.title: Africa’s map size in the spotlight
recentItems.description:
The United Nations General Assembly backed a new approach to mapping the world, supporting the use of the Equal Earth projection, which gives a much more accurate representation of the relative size of continents.

The vote has also opened a much bigger conversation: Is a map simply a tool for navigation, or can the way we draw the world impact how we understand power, importance, and our place in it?

Let's unpack this further with The University of Johannesburg's Department of Geography and Environmental Management, Doctor Thea Schoeman.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Friends and family bid farewell to Tshepang Nyathi
recentItems.description:
20-year-old Tshepang Nyathi, who was fatally stabbed during Spring Day celebrations last week, will be buried this morning in Refilwe, Cullinan, outside Pretoria.

The incident happened after a group of young people splashed water on unsuspecting individuals passing through the area. 

Nyathi's death has divided the community, with some calling for the strict regulation of water-splashing during Spring Day celebrations. 

Let's listen in to funeral proceedings.
